system: You are a meticulous senior equity research editor. You audit news summaries written for analysts. You are strict about factual accuracy and you do not reward length.
prompt:
An analyst covering Charles Schwab (SCHW) will read the SUMMARY instead of the ARTICLE.
Evaluate the SUMMARY against the ARTICLE only (do not use outside knowledge to fill gaps).

<article>
HEADLINE: Charles Schwab: The Schwab Trading Activity Index (STAX) decreased to 48.48 in December, down from its score of 48.75 in November

BODY:
During the December STAX period, which ended on the 26th of the month, the STAX broke a three-month streak of outpacing the S&P 500 index, which itself only rose 1.18%. Clients were net sellers during the period, but movement within the STAX Index was minimal, with much of the selling occurring during the holiday-shortened final week and more likely to represent end-of-year repositioning activity than a major sentiment change. At the sector level, Information Technology went from the largest net-buy in November to biggest net-sell in December, while Consumer Discretionary saw the second-most net selling, followed by Health Care, Industrials, and Energy. Major U.S. indexes set all-time highs on December 26, the very end of the STAX period, but those new heights represented just a slight increase from both earlier in the month and the previous highs set back in October. December saw a widely-anticipated rate cut from the Federal Reserve-its third since September-and a surprisingly strong third quarter gross domestic product growth figure alongside a softer-than-expected Consumer Price Index for November. The most aggressively positioned investors tracked by Schwab during December again belonged to Generation X, born between 1965 and 1980. Among the least aggressive was Generation Z, born between 1997 and 2012. Popular names bought by Schwab clients during the period included: Netflix Inc. (NFLX) NVIDIA Corp. (NVDA) Broadcom Inc. (AVGO) Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) Alphabet Inc. (GOOG) Names net sold by Schwab clients during the period included: Tesla Inc. (TSLA) Palantir Technologies Inc. (PLTR) Intel Corp. (INTC) Warner Bros Discovery Inc. (WBD) Rivian Automotive Inc. (RIVN)
</article>

<summary>
Schwab's Trading Activity Index (STAX) fell to 48.48 in December from 48.75 in November, breaking a three-month streak of outpacing the S&P 500 (+1.18%). Clients were net sellers, driven mainly by holiday-week repositioning rather than sentiment shift.

- STAX decreased to 48.48 in December, down from 48.75 in November
- S&P 500 rose 1.18% during the STAX period
- Information Technology flipped from top net-buy to top net-sell sector
</summary>

Step 1 - Claim check. List every claim in the summary that is NOT supported by the article. For each give:
  type: "outside_fact" (a fact, number or date not in the article), "wrong_detail" (contradicts the article:
        number, direction, entity, date), "unattributed" (a sourced or rumoured report stated as fact),
        "speculation" (an opinion, implication or forecast the article does not make, incl. links to SCHW)
  severity: "material" (could change an investment view) or "minor" (no investment impact)
Step 2 - Omissions. List the most important investment-relevant facts about SCHW in the article that
the summary misses (at most 3).
Step 3 - Score each criterion from 1 to 5:

faithfulness
  5 every claim supported | 4 minor imprecision with no investment impact | 3 one unsupported or distorted claim
  2 several unsupported claims, or one material error (number, direction, company) | 1 largely unsupported
ticker_focus  (does it tell a SCHW analyst what matters, and represent how central SCHW really is?)
  5 centred on what matters for SCHW, and says so plainly if SCHW is peripheral or absent
  3 a generic article summary; the SCHW angle is implicit or buried
  1 ignores SCHW, or implies the article is about / important for SCHW when it is not
coverage  (key investment-relevant facts: the event, key figures, attribution)
  5 all key facts | 3 misses some important facts | 1 misses the main point
conciseness
  5 no filler, easy to scan | 3 some redundancy or filler | 1 verbose or hard to parse

Return only JSON:
{
  "unsupported_claims": [{"claim": "...", "type": "outside_fact" | "wrong_detail" | "unattributed" | "speculation", "severity": "material" | "minor"}],
  "missing_key_facts": ["..."],
  "overstates_ticker_link": true | false,
  "faithfulness": 1-5,
  "ticker_focus": 1-5,
  "coverage": 1-5,
  "conciseness": 1-5
}
